title: Bhir Mound: the earlier Taxila
alt: Low stone walls and irregular building remains at Bhir Mound
caption: Bhir Mound, photographed December 2008. This is the early settlement component of Taxila, not the later planned city of Sirkap. Individual exposed walls are not assigned to Alexander's visit in 326 BCE. Modern pylons and buildings belong to the present landscape.
modifications: No local edits; original or publisher/Commons-provided derivative as downloaded.

title: Northern Black Polished Ware from Sonkh
alt: Dark polished pottery fragment held by modern display supports
caption: Government Museum, Mathura, showcase 6-15; Sonkh fragment with a museum-photo attribution of 500-100 BCE, photographed 24 February 2013. That broad object range extends beyond this scene's urbanisation window. No excavation layer or exact manufacture year is inferred.
modifications: No local edits; original or publisher/Commons-provided derivative as downloaded.

title: Kumrahar: a surviving hall pillar
alt: Broken stone pillar displayed horizontally under a modern shelter at Kumrahar
caption: Mauryan hall pillar at Kumrahar, Patna, uploaded 3 November 2008; capture date unverified. This architectural fragment gives material context for Pataliputra. The shelter and supports are modern; the photograph does not establish the hall's precise function or reconstruct the entire building.
modifications: No local edits; original or publisher/Commons-provided derivative as downloaded.

title: Sudama: the worked stone surface
alt: Close interior view of smooth curved granite wall and ceiling at Sudama cave
caption: Sudama Cave interior detail, photographed 6 October 2023. The curved surfaces show the treatment of the living rock; this close view is not a measured plan of its two chambers. Modern surface marks should not be read as an Ashokan inscription.
modifications: No local edits; original or publisher/Commons-provided derivative as downloaded.

title: Sarnath: the lion capital
alt: Back-to-back carved lions above a wheel-and-animal abacus and bell-shaped base
caption: Sarnath Museum: Ashokan lion capital, conventionally dated about 250 BCE. Photograph record dated 9 July 2011; Commons publishes a detail view. This is the surviving capital, not the complete pillar or a photograph of an edict.
credit: Chrisi1964; published detail via Wikimedia Commons
modifications: No local edits; original or publisher/Commons-provided derivative as downloaded.

title: Lumbini: detail of the Brahmi inscription
alt: Lines of Brahmi letters cut into the curved stone surface of the Lumbini pillar
caption: Photographed 12 March 2013 by Anandajoti / Photo Dharma. This close view complements the whole-pillar photograph. It shows part of the inscription on a curved surface, not a complete flat transcription; consult the linked edition for missing edges and line readings.
modifications: No local edits; original or publisher/Commons-provided derivative as downloaded.

title: Girnar: Major Rock Edict XIII
alt: Historical printed facsimile of Girnar Edict XIII with line numbers and damaged areas
caption: Published facsimile of the Girnar version of Major Rock Edict XIII, via the Commons extraction from the Girnar plate. This is an editorial record of the inscription, not a modern photograph of the rock. Damage and line numbering remain visible; it is distinct from Dhauli's separate Kalinga edicts.
credit: Alexander Cunningham / Eugen Hultzsch, historical plate via Wikimedia Commons
modifications: No local edits; original or publisher/Commons-provided derivative as downloaded.

title: Shahbazgarhi: Edicts VII and XII
alt: Published inscription plate headed Seventh and Twelfth Rock Edicts Shahbazgarhi
caption: Eugen Hultzsch, Inscriptions of Asoka (1925): Shahbazgarhi Edicts VII and XII in Kharosthi. The page preserves the edition's labels and line numbers. It documents two specified texts, not a generic alphabet chart or a Greek/Aramaic inscription.

title: Gandhara: a bent-bar comparison
alt: Elongated bent-bar coin with separate punched marks in a museum display
caption: INHCRF Coin Museum, Nashik; identified in the photographer's record as a Gandhara bent-bar type. Photograph dated 31 July 2026, not an ancient event date. Accession, mass and the individual specimen's date remain unverified; do not transfer the British Museum coin's measurements to it.

title: Mahavira: a 15th-century painted witness
alt: Painted panel showing Mahavira at the centre of a circular preaching assembly
caption: The Met, 55.121.38.18, Gujarat, 15th century CE: painted detail from a Kalpasutra folio, ink, opaque watercolour and gold on paper. This later devotional image represents Mahavira's samavasarana; it is not a contemporary portrait or a picture made in the sixth century BCE.
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1955
modifications: No local edits; original or publisher/Commons-provided derivative as downloaded.

title: The first sermon: an 11th-century interpretation
alt: Black stone Buddha seated with hands in a teaching gesture on a lotus base
caption: The Met, 20.43, Bihar, probably Nalanda, 11th century CE. This Pala-period sculpture interprets the first sermon at Sarnath. It is a later work about the Buddha, not an object from his lifetime; its place of production differs from the place represented.
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1920
